text: Postmortem of last week's outage: a config push set the connection pool max to 0 because an empty string was parsed as zero. Our validator checked for null, not empty. Fixes: parse-don't-validate for config, canary config rollouts, and alert on pool-wait time rather than error rate, which stayed flat during the incident because requests queued instead of failing.

text: Coding-agent benchmarks mostly measure whether a hidden test suite passes, which rewards narrow patches. In our internal evaluation of 200 real PRs, 31% of 'passing' agent patches were rejected by reviewers for changing behavior outside the issue. Pass rate without reviewer acceptance overstates usefulness.

text: I don't think AI eliminates 'jobs'; it re-bundles tasks. In customer support, the share of tickets resolved without humans rose from 22% to 41% at our company, but the remaining tickets are harder, so headcount fell only 8% while required seniority rose. The risk is to the entry-level pipeline, not the occupation.

label: highlight
text: Why did housing prices keep rising despite higher rates? Most existing owners hold sub-4% fixed mortgages, so they won't sell (the lock-in effect), which cut the supply of existing homes sharply. Rates are suppressing transactions, not prices. That is why any relief should show up first in volume, not price.

text: Paper summary: position effects in long contexts. The authors show retrieval accuracy drops about 20 points when the relevant passage sits mid-context in 20-document prompts. Practical implication: rank first, then place the best evidence at the start or end. Caveat: tested on older models, and newer ones may show smaller effects.

text: The new JWST result on early-galaxy brightness doesn't break cosmology the way headlines say. The galaxies are bright, but the mass estimates carry large uncertainty from dust and bursty star formation; at the stated error bars most of the tension disappears with a modest increase in star-formation efficiency.

text: Why I expect the filibuster change to backfire: in 2013 and 2017 the 'nuclear option' expanded majority power at the time, and the precedent then stayed available to opponents. text: I think there's a real risk that code review becomes the bottleneck as AI-assisted code volume rises. At our org PR count rose 38% in a year while reviewer headcount was flat, and median time-to-review went from 6h to 19h. Unless review tooling or norms change, the throughput gains will be absorbed there.

label: highlight
text: Three ways idempotency keys fail in practice: (1) keys scoped per client rather than per operation, so retries with a changed payload silently return stale results; (2) TTLs shorter than your longest retry window; (3) storing the key after the side effect rather than atomically with it. Fix: persist key and request hash in the same transaction as the effect, and reject mismatched hashes with a 422.

The problem isn't bad faith; it's that no shared protocol exists.
